articles.title: GardenBench: A lightweight, daily evaluation of LLM capabilities
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce GardenBench, a benchmark with 11 test suites that evaluate the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) across a range of tasks. By systematically prompting LLMs with various lightweight queries, we document day-to-day changes in model performance, including run costs and times, that other benchmarks miss. This allows us to compare the accuracy and features of responses across model providers and versions. articles.title: Doing Less with More: A First-Principles Exploration of the Suitability of Agentic Computing over Alternative Architectural Choices
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There is growing interest in automating business activities with Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) due to latter's seeming ease of use. Never has it been easier, or costlier, to do less with more. However, little is known about when agents are preferable to established alternatives such as local computation, Representational State Transfer (REST), the Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP), and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), particularly when development speed, performance, and operational cost are considered. articles.title: A Controlled LLM Workflow for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis of Risk Score Differences
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a controlled Large Language Model (LLM) workflow for explaining risk score differences using similar historical transactions. The workflow combines reference retrieval and contrastive SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) evidence with reference-based LLM reasoning and deterministic validation. Experiments on a test dataset show that the workflow produces more consistent, evidence-grounded and traceable diagnoses than the same LLM without structured workflow guidance.

articles.title: What Social Media Teaches Us About Accumulative AI Risks
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.24006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prominent AI safety discussions emphasize existential threats and catastrophic events, such as AI-enabled nuclear conflict or engineered biological outbreaks. This position paper argues that there is another type of AI risk that arises and accumulates from the widespread use of AI. Drawing on lessons from social media, we argue that safety assessments must also address accumulative harms that develop through repeated use, recurring decisions, and feedback across interconnected deployments. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intelligent agent interactions in real-world web environments are commonly constrained by request budgets, time delays, anti-crawling restrictions, and operational failure risks. articles.title: PolyGraph: Plan-Buffered CUDA Graphs for Adaptive Speculative Decoding
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive speculative decoding changes the active batch size B and draft length d from one decode step to the next, whereas a CUDA Graph replays a fixed launch configuration. The resulting verification width M = B d forces serving systems to pre-capture many shapes, capture new ones on the serving path, or pad every step to the largest draft. We present PolyGraph, a plan-buffer mechanism for custom Triton kernels that avoids this choice. PolyGraph captures one maximum-grid graph and writes the active shape to GPU memory before each replay. Kernels

articles.summary: arXiv:2610.25061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncovering low-dimensional representations of brain-wide neural dynamics and their relationship to behavior remains a central challenge. articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? articles.title: People who are more considerate of others show less “me first” bias in quick decisions
articles.summary: People usually recognize their own belongings faster than someone else’s, even when the items are just pens and pencils. A study found this self-bias was weaker among people who were more attentive to others’ needs and choices.

articles.title: People with darker personalities tend to prefer partners like themselves, study suggests
articles.summary: Why are some people drawn to manipulative or even violent partners? In a study of 400 Brazilian adults, those with darker personality traits tended to rate similar traits as more desirable in a romantic partner.

articles.title: Your body’s state may shape whether your best ideas are verbal or visual
articles.summary: Not all creativity may draw on the same bodily state. In a study that tracked students’ hearts for five days, calmer physiological states went with more original drawings but less original verbal ideas.

articles.title: Brain connectivity patterns map onto sensory processing styles in autistic youth
articles.summary: Machine learning analysis reveals that different sensory experiences in autistic children correspond to unique patterns of brain connectivity. The research highlights how distinct brain networks shape the way individuals perceive and interact with the physical world.
